A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BALLAST and VaSE research. All 24 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–I, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Sections 5.1–5.3 and Appendix H report original simulated drifter deployments, policy comparisons, and ablations using synthetic Helmholtz fields and SUNTANS outputs.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds measured runtimes and experiments on discretisation, surrogate choice, and flow evolution in Sections 4.1–4.2 and H.3–H.5.

M1.justification: The BALLAST acquisition, trajectory simulation procedure, and VaSE regression and propagation steps remain unchanged in Section 4 and Algorithms 1–2. The alternative RBF surrogate is an experimental ablation of the existing procedure, whose compatibility with different surrogates was already stated.

E1.justification: Synthetic Helmholtz and SUNTANS coverage is retained. Appendix H.5 extends the synthetic test scenarios to flows evolving rapidly or slowly, using temporal lengthscales 0.5 and 5.0 around the original 2.5.

E2.justification: v3 adds an empirical timing comparison against SPDE, previously compared only through complexity expressions, and evaluates the EIG-mis variant in the new surrogate ablation. The six-policy comparison in Figures 6–7 retains UNIF, SOBOL, DIST-SEP, EIG, BALLAST-opt, and BALLAST-true.

E3.justification: New experiments vary forward projection steps across 0.01, 0.05, and 0.1, equip EIG and BALLAST with independent vector-output RBF surrogates, and measure runtimes at selected decision times. The original benchmark grids, deployment schedules, and L2-based rank and iso-performance evaluation remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix H expands beyond sample-number and projection-horizon tuning to test numerical discretisation sensitivity, dependence on the surrogate, and failure conditions associated with slow flow evolution. These three new analyses substantially broaden robustness and mechanism testing while retaining H.1–H.2.

E5.justification: The existing ten synthetic fields with ten runs each, 100 seeded SUNTANS runs, and two-standard-error bounds are retained. The added tables and timings introduce no explicit new repetition counts, uncertainty estimates, or statistical tests.

E6.justification: v3 substantially expands reported results with timings and Tables 2–4. Examples include VaSE versus SPDE sampling times of 3.89 versus 259.83 seconds at t=5, utility gaps below 1% for all tested steps at J=20, and BALLAST-mis consistently outranking EIG-mis. Table 4 adds a boundary finding: at n=19, BALLAST/SOBOL ranks are 1.05/2.25 for rapid evolution but 1.55/1.45 for slow evolution. Existing plotted results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix B.3 corrects the independent-variable identity from H(X,Y)=H(X)H(Y) to H(X,Y)=H(X)+H(Y). The propositions, proofs, and VaSE complexity derivations otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about trajectory-aware active learning, VaSE sampling efficiency, and improved drifter placement. The additions provide supporting evidence without redefining these central contributions.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the new analyses as evidence of discretisation robustness and a look-ahead benefit beyond the Helmholtz surrogate, and identifies slowly evolving flows as a regime with weaker advantages. The impact statement also replaces generic wording with environmental applications and possible oil and gas uses.

D1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 disclose an Apple Silicon CPU and 24 GB RAM for the new timings. H.3 newly specifies 0.05 as the forward projection default; the 0.01 ground-truth trajectory integration in I.1 is retained. Existing software, cluster, and code-access information remains available.

R1.justification: The cited works and central research positioning are retained. Qing et al. changes from a 2024 preprint citation to its 2025 TMLR publication, representing the same work; the other reference edits concern bibliographic formatting or metadata.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized grammar and notation edits, updates author order, affiliations, and publication information, and rewrites the impact statement. New appendix subsections accompany the experiments, but the existing narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Three compact tables are added as Tables 2–4. All ten figure images and Table 1 are retained; several figures, including Figures 2, 4–5, and 8, are repositioned as text reflows within the existing two-column layout.

improvement.justification: Measured runtimes make practical feasibility more assessable, while H.3–H.5 add useful controls for discretisation and surrogate dependence and identify a concrete applicability boundary. The entropy correction also improves accuracy. These strengthen the existing paper, although the absence of uncertainty estimates for the new tables and timings limits the strength of the added conclusions.
